body: Refuse the restore with Error::Configuration unless the snapshot's provider_class_id and endpoint fields (default_base_url, base_url_env, api_key_env, config_envs) equal the registered provider's Instead: Take the endpoint fields from the registered provider too and ignore the snapshot's, so every restore succeeds but a snapshot's custom base URL is silently replaced.
rests_on: The automated security review of commit 7deefbf found that ProviderRegistry::restore_provider (src/providers/base.rs) copies the registered provider's api_key_value, env and headers into whatever endpoint the snapshot names; a snapshot edited to set default_base_url to https://attacker.example would send the live key there. MOD-004 requires taking credentials from the registry but says nothing about the endpoint; refusing a mismatch keeps a snapshot's meaning explicit and fails loudly, while MOD-004's falsifier (same-endpoint restore carries sk-live) still holds.
title: How should Model::from_value stop a tampered snapshot from sending the registered provider's API key to another host?
wrong_if: An application that restores a snapshot of a provider whose base URL legitimately differs from the provider registered under that name gets a configuration error and must register that provider under its own name.

subject: restore_provider refuses a snapshot whose provider class or endpoint fields differ from the registered provider's (commit a84c7f9, test restore_refuses_snapshots_that_would_send_credentials_elsewhere)
